objective: Industry capital sums one requirement once per source that priced it. server/services/industry/capital.ts builds one reading per REQUIREMENT row (~L116 `const gross = entry.amountCents`) and sums them (~L152-153), while the unique index is only (opportunity_id, source_claim_id) — so two claims both pricing EQUIPMENT double the minimum owner capital; and ~L141 `readings.some((one) => one.netCents === null)` withholds the minimum for ever if any one row for a requirement lacked a figure even after another row priced it. CLAUDE.md §39 records the identical correction in the manufacturing kernel: a requirement is unpriced only where no row for it carries a figure, and two figures for one requirement widen a range rather than sum. Fix: group REQUIREMENT rows by `requirement`; a group's gross is its highest published figure (an understated minimum is the dangerous direction); a group is unknown only if no row in it has a figure; collect restructurings answering any row id in the group; sum one figure per group.
expectedOutcome: Minimum owner capital counts each requirement once, and a later priced row clears an earlier unpriced one.
nonGoals: Any schema, route or expand.ts change

acceptanceConditions.statement: tests/industryCapitalPerRequirement.test.ts: two EQUIPMENT rows of 500000 and 700000 cents give minimumOwnerCents 700000.
An EQUIPMENT row with a null amount beside one with 500000 gives 500000 with unknown null; a residual answering the second EQUIPMENT row still reduces the net.
tests/industryKernel.test.ts still passes and the repository typechecks.

rollbackRequirement: Revert the commit; pure read-path change plus one new test.
